Title: The Island
Comment:
This song was written in 1985, but it feels as real and as relevant now as it did then.

It sings about war in Lebanon, women and children dying on TV. After 40 years, nothing has really changed. It talks about the great cedar forests burning. Back then it must have seemed unimaginable that our world would heat up but it feels like a new harsh reality.

The conflicts have changed, but the hatred is still there. In the North, it's taken different forms through Islamophobia, xenophobia, and families being burnt out of their homes It doesn't take much to see that nationalism has taken new forms.

But this isn't meant to be a sad post...

In a world that can feel full of suffering, I've been lucky enough to find love, on an island. I only half knew this girl before stepping on a small Island and after a few days I had completely fallen for her. There's something about the Irish islands that gives me a sense of peace. I feel calm, safe and present there. The world slows and my mind with it.

Title: Blackbird
Comment:
My Grandad used to love road tripping in Ireland. Sharon Shannon was one of his favourite artists & I still remember being in the back of the car when I was young listening to this song as we drove through the mountains.
They say with dementia it’s like grieving someone twice, once when they lose their memory & again once they pass away. I used to love spending time with him, even if we had the same conversations over & over again, and even when he forgot who I was. I always just wished I could have one more proper conversation with the man I once knew, tell him about all the exciting things in my life as I knew he would be so happy for me. Playing this song was one way to break back into his mind & catch a glimpse of his old self. He would turn to me & smile, & his foot would tap away to the beat. I would play it every time I was at his house, & sometimes multiple times a day. It would cheer us both up & bring back happy memories of the drives through the mountains. Forever loved x

Title: All My Friends Are Falling In Love
Album: All My Friends Are Falling In Love
Comment:
My alarm is the radio and this song was what played when I woke up on the first day in my new house 

Then I played it as I made breakfast with my new housemates, ran out the door of my new neighbourhood, chatted in the coffee shop, and then joined the hoards of cyclists to work in the city as the autumn leaves trickled on my pretty new streets 

To me this song feels like the beginning of a romcom buddy movie. I used to think it was a song of jealousy and now hearing it I feel a song of beginnings - all my friends are fall-ING in love yaaaay! So much is going to happen :)

Title: New York, I Love You but You're Bringing Me Down
Comment:
I watched this live, and a certain someone in the squad became quite emotional during the performance. Although the song itself is mainly about the gentrification of NY, for them it brought back memories of a time when their gang was leaving college and all taking separate paths into adulthood.

As I start a new chapter myself, I can't help but have similar feelings while listening — comforted by the fact that, during a possible few spells of loneliness ahead, I'll still be connected to my group, even if only by sending a few tunes to one another.
